title: Curation update: cGAS-STING activation by mitochondrial DNA release
subtitle: Proposed additions to an existing Reactome pathway from a single primary paper - pre-curation draft for curator review
author: Marc Gillespie (St. John's University)

target_pathway.name: STING mediated induction of host immune responses

source_paper.citation: Kim J, Gupta R, Blanco LP, Yang S, Shteinfer-Kuzmine A, Wang K, Zhu J, Yoon HE, Wang X, Kerkhofs M, Kang H, Brown AL, Park SJ, Xu X, Zandee van Rilland E, Kim MK, Cohen JI, Kaplan MJ, Shoshan-Barmatz V, Chung JH. VDAC oligomers form mitochondrial pores to release mtDNA fragments and promote lupus-like disease. Science 366 (2019): 1531-1536.

summary: The target pathway currently models cGAS sensing of cytosolic double-stranded DNA, STING trafficking from the ER to the ERGIC, TBK1 recruitment, and IRF3 phosphorylation, but it treats the source of the cytosolic DNA as an unspecified input.

This paper provides direct experimental evidence that VDAC1/VDAC3 oligomerisation forms a mitochondrial outer-membrane pore through which mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) fragments reach the cytosol, and that this released mtDNA is sufficient to activate cGAS in the absence of any exogenous DNA.
Two new reaction-like events and two new physical entities are proposed. No existing event needs to be retired; one existing reaction gains a defined input and a new preceding event.
rationale: Reactome curates at the reaction level, so an upstream source of a previously unspecified input is best represented as explicit new events rather than as a note on the existing reaction. Adding the VDAC pore formation step and the mtDNA translocation step gives the existing cGAS activation reaction a proper precedingEvent chain.

The VDAC1:VDAC3 oligomer is represented as a new Complex rather than as a DefinedSet because the paper demonstrates a specific heteromeric stoichiometry by native PAGE and crosslinking, not functional interchangeability of the two subunits.
Both proposed events are human (HEK293T, THP-1, and primary human fibroblasts), so neither is chimeric and neither requires an inferred-from annotation.

gap_analysis.what_the_paper_changes: REFINES — Input dsDNA is currently a generic cytosolic DNA entity with no defined origin. The paper identifies released mtDNA as a physiological source; add the new mtDNA entity as an additional input candidate and set the new translocation reaction as a preceding event.
CONFIRMS — no change to the reaction itself. The paper supplies additional human evidence that could be added as a second literature reference on the existing event.

new_entities.notes: Heteromeric pore; paper reports a predominant hexameric species by BN-PAGE (Fig. 2a). Component UniProt accessions pending curator verification.
new_entities.status: NEW - needs creation in the Curator Tool

new_entities.notes: Represented as a single OtherEntity rather than a GenomeEncodedEntity because the paper characterises a heterogeneous fragment population, not a defined locus.
new_entities.reuses: Possible reuse of an existing cytosolic mtDNA entity - check gk_central before creating

new_events.label: RXN-1
new_events.name: VDAC1 and VDAC3 oligomerise in the mitochondrial outer membrane
regulators: negatively regulated by VBIT-4 (small-molecule VDAC oligomerisation inhibitor)
new_events.go_bp: GO:0097191 extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway (candidate - curator to confirm)
new_events.summation: Oxidative stress induced by rotenone or by mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM) depletion promotes the oligomerisation of VDAC1 and VDAC3 within the mitochondrial outer membrane. The resulting hetero-oligomeric pore is detected by blue native PAGE and by chemical crosslinking in human fibroblasts, and its formation is blocked by the VDAC oligomerisation inhibitor VBIT-4.
new_events.evidence_sentence: Blue native PAGE of digitonin-solubilised mitochondria from rotenone-treated human fibroblasts resolved a VDAC1- and VDAC3-containing species of approximately 190 kDa that was absent from VBIT-4-treated cells.
flags: Modelled as a BlackBoxEvent because the oligomer stoichiometry is not fully resolved.
GO BP term is a candidate only - needs OLS confirmation.

new_events.label: RXN-2
new_events.name: Mitochondrial DNA fragments translocate to the cytosol through the VDAC1:VDAC3 pore
new_events.catalyst: VDAC1:VDAC3 oligomer (GO:0015267 channel activity - pending verification)
new_events.preceding_event: RXN-1 - VDAC1 and VDAC3 oligomerise in the mitochondrial outer membrane
new_events.summation: Mitochondrial DNA fragments of 500-700 bp pass from the mitochondrial matrix into the cytosol through the VDAC1:VDAC3 hetero-oligomeric pore. Cytosolic mtDNA is quantified by subcellular fractionation followed by qPCR against mitochondrial loci, and its appearance requires VDAC oligomerisation.
new_events.evidence_sentence: Cytosolic fractions from rotenone-treated THP-1 cells contained a 14-fold enrichment of mtDNA relative to untreated controls, an effect abolished by VBIT-4 and by combined VDAC1/VDAC3 knockdown.

open_questions.question: Should the cytosolic mtDNA fragment reuse an existing Reactome entity, or is a new OtherEntity warranted? Check gk_central for a cytosolic mtDNA entity before creating one.
Is BlackBoxEvent the right class for RXN-1, or should the oligomer be built as a defined Complex with explicit stoichiometry once the hexameric assignment is confirmed?
Does the existing cGAS binding reaction (R-HSA-3249367) need a second literature reference, or is the new preceding event enough to capture this paper's contribution?

checklist: Every PMID in this document resolved against NCBI E-utilities, not from training data.
gk_central checked for pre-existing VDAC1:VDAC3 and cytosolic mtDNA entities.
All GO accessions confirmed in OLS4 and recorded with their current labels.
UniProt accessions for VDAC1 and VDAC3 confirmed (human, reviewed).
Compartment assignments match Curator Guide V94 conventions.
Summations reviewed for Reactome house style (present tense, no citation markers in body text).
Preceding-event chain verified end to end against the existing pathway.
